subject: Request: downstream vendor authority & evidence for cross-border processing
messages:
From: Linda Park <linda@securebank.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: privacyops@securebank.com
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Downstream vendor authority and cross-border evidence request

Hi Ben,

Following our procurement review, SecureBank needs confirmation about a downstream analytics partner that may receive logged inference telemetry from your hosted runtime. Please confirm the following items so we can close our transfer risk assessment: 

1) A current list of sub-processors that may access production telemetry or aggregated logs (name, country, role, effective date).
2) The legal transfer mechanism for each non-EEA sub-processor (SCCs, adequacy decision, or other).
3) Whether any sub-processor onward-transfers data to third parties and, if so, who and why.
4) A short DPIA or DPIA summary for the analytics flow (or pointer to where we can review it).
5) The date of the most recent change to the roster and whether any changes since 2026-01-01 were material.

We appreciate a response within 3 business days. If there are any planned changes that would require SecureBank review/consent, please flag them explicitly. Our legal & privacy teams are sensitive to US-bound analytics pipelines and will require SCC references and a copy of the encryption/key management flow where applicable.

Thanks,

Linda Park
Lead Privacy Counsel, SecureBank PLC
privacyops@securebank.com

Attachments referenced: none (please provide attachments in your reply)

Ben / Laura —

Attached is the current roster extract and a short DPIA summary for the telemetry pipeline. High level: we use an analytics partner (DataVista LLC, US) to process aggregated SDK metrics and non-identifiable telemetry for capacity planning and model quality signals. 

Key points (summary):
- DataVista receives only aggregated event batches (no raw prompt contents). We apply prefix KV redaction and token truncation before export.
- Transfer mechanism: Standard EU Commission SCCs (2021 clauses) are in place for DataVista; signed annex available on request.
- Most recent roster change: 2026-01-05 (added DataVista for pilot), change logged in the vendor ledger. We consider this a material change for privacy reviewers.
- DPIA summary attached (see attachments) — mitigation includes encryption-in-transit, per-customer pseudonymization, and retention limits (30 days for telemetry batches).

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_roster_20260212.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
